At the start, Allen got away very fast with Bert Clayton close on his heels and the rest of our boys well up filling various positions from George Oliver 15 to Tony Bellchamber 60.

In 1914 a young Belgravian named Jimmy Bellchamber determined that the Club’s colours should be prominently carried over the 52 miles of road that year, but the outbreak of war caused a postponement of plans.
In the absence of our leading scratch men, Tony Bellchamber carried the Club colours with great credit and in finishing 17th out of 149 starters, was our first man home.
